svg.title: Finite CAR modes and recovery by product-state expectations
svg.desc: Two occupation modes have parity-corrected commuting matrix legs. Their tracial GNS expectations retain one leg and average the other. In a general product state, the expectation tower of an inner implementer gives an exact overlap product tending to one.
svg.text: Parity, finite slices and the overlap tail
1. Two modes in the occupation basis
H_Fock = C² ⊗ C²; b = |0⟩⟨1|; Z = diag(1, −1)
a₁ = b ⊗ I; a₂ = Z ⊗ b
{aᵢ, aⱼ*} = δᵢⱼ I; {aᵢ, aⱼ} = 0
b₁ = a₁; b₂ = (Z ⊗ I)a₂ = I ⊗ b
The b-legs commute; each leg generates M₂.
Together they generate M₂ ⊗ M₂ = M₄.
2. A finite tracial expectation
Ωⱼ = I₂ / √2 ∈ S₂(C²); τⱼ(x) = Tr(x) / 2
Use left multiplication on Hτ = S₂(C²) ⊗ S₂(C²).
uⱼ = diag(eⁱᶿʲ, e⁻ⁱᶿʲ); U = u₁ ⊗ u₂
U
E₁
cos(θ₂) u₁ ⊗ I
E₀(U) = (√2 / 4) I; Ω = Ω₁ ⊗ Ω₂
3. The full product-state innerness mechanism
α = Ad(u); vₙ = u₁ ⋯ uₙ; wₙ = vₙ* u ∈ M_tail
Eₙ(u) = aₙvₙ; aₙ = ω(wₙ); rⱼ = ωⱼ(uⱼ) ≥ 0
EₙEₘ = Eₙ ⇒ aₙ = aₘ ∏ⱼ₌ₙ₊₁ᵐ rⱼ
Eₙ(u)Ω → uΩ ⇒ |aₙ| → 1
For late n: ∏ (j > n) rⱼ = |aₙ| > 0
Σ (j > n) (1 − rⱼ) ≤ −log|aₙ| → 0
Mⱼ factors; αⱼ preserve their normal states ωⱼ.
CAR Theorem 2.1 · ITP Theorems 4.1 and 7.2 · CC0
